newsitem.title: GERMANY: New drugs help Boehringer Ingelheim sales jump.
newsitem.headline: New drugs help Boehringer Ingelheim sales jump.

text.p: German pharmaceuticals and chemicals group Boehringer Ingelheim said on Tuesday stronger volume sales as well as new products helped boost sales 6.8 percent in the first half of the year.

The 111-year-old family-held company, currently ranked number 20 in the world, said sales rose to 3.4 billion marks ($2.3 billion) in the first half of 1996 with prescription drug sales making up the lion's share of total sales.
For the year as a whole, Boehringer Ingelheim was optimistic that sales could total seven billion marks, which would translate into a nearly nine percent rise from 1995's 6.43 billion mark sales.
But Boehringer cautioned that this outlook depended largely on currency rates remaining stable.

Last year, the mark's strength as compared with the dollar and other European currencies was largely responsible for denting sales and profits at many German companies, particularly pharmaceutical companies which exported drugs abroad.
The group did not disclose profit figures.

Among Boehringer Ingelheim's various business units, prescription drugs sales rose six percent to 2.86 billion marks in the first half with animal health sales surging 53 percent to 176 million marks.
Meanwhile the group's chemical sales dropped by eight percent to 215 million marks and sales in the baking and foods business stagnated at 169 million marks.
The group also said that acquisitions had helped boost sales by 1.5 percent during the first half of the year.

Meanwhile Boehringer Ingelheim, considered by many analysts to have a promising drugs pipeline and the knack of turning new research into profitable products, said it had boosted spending on research and development by 15 percent to 578 million marks in the first half of the year.
